A listing and its summary in one table: plan_append()

Source: vignettes/articles/plan-append.Rmd
plan-append.Rmd

In Japanese

A PK concentration table often lists every subject’s concentrations by time point and, under them on the same columns, their summary statistics. The two parts come from two sources – the records and an ARD of their statistics – but they are one table: one column header, one set of column widths, and a page for each analyte and treatment that holds both parts of that group.

In rtfreporter each part is an ordinary plan, and plan_append() lays the rows of the second under the rows of the first. This page builds such a table for a fictional study.

library(rtfreporter)

The data

A fictional study of Example Pharma: Drug A at 100 mg and 200 mg, six subjects each, plasma concentrations of Drug A and its metabolite M1 at seven nominal times after the dose. The lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ) is 2.00 ng/mL; a sample below it is BLQ (AVAL missing). Every pre-dose sample is BLQ, so the table starts at 0.5 h.

Show code 
set.seed(20261102)
subj <- data.frame(USUBJID = as.character(1001:1012),
                   ARM = rep(c("Drug A 100 mg", "Drug A 200 mg"), each = 6),
                   AGE = sample(28:64, 12, replace = TRUE),
                   SEX = sample(c("M", "F"), 12, replace = TRUE),
                   dose = rep(c(100, 200), each = 6))
tpt <- data.frame(ATPTN = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24),
                  ATPT = c("0.5", "1", "2", "4", "8", "12", "24"))
analyte <- data.frame(ANALYTE = c("Drug A", "Metabolite M1"),
                      frac = c(1, 0.3), ke = c(0.17, 0.09))
adpc <- merge(merge(subj, tpt, by = NULL), analyte, by = NULL)
conc <- with(adpc, frac * dose * 0.9 * 1.4 / (1.4 - ke) *
                     (exp(-ke * ATPTN) - exp(-1.4 * ATPTN)))
conc <- conc * stats::rlnorm(nrow(adpc), 0, 0.25)
adpc$AVAL <- ifelse(conc < 2, NA_real_, signif(conc, 3))   # BLQ: missing
adpc <- adpc[order(adpc$ANALYTE, adpc$ARM, adpc$USUBJID, adpc$ATPTN),
             c("USUBJID", "ARM", "AGE", "SEX", "ANALYTE", "ATPT", "AVAL")]
head(adpc)
#>    USUBJID           ARM AGE SEX ANALYTE ATPT AVAL
#> 1     1001 Drug A 100 mg  33   M  Drug A  0.5 42.6
#> 13    1001 Drug A 100 mg  33   M  Drug A    1 47.8
#> 25    1001 Drug A 100 mg  33   M  Drug A    2 62.8
#> 37    1001 Drug A 100 mg  33   M  Drug A    4 39.5
#> 49    1001 Drug A 100 mg  33   M  Drug A    8 28.9
#> 61    1001 Drug A 100 mg  33   M  Drug A   12 10.9

The two parts

The listing is a plan on the records: a row a subject, a column a time point, the concentration in each cell. The row label puts the subject’s ID, age and sex together (1001/33/M); a BLQ sample prints BLQ. The concentrations print to three significant digits, as reported.

Show code 
listing <- adpc |>
  table_plan(cols = "ATPT", rows = c(subject = ~ "{USUBJID}/{AGE}/{SEX}"),
             value = "AVAL") |>
  plan_cells("{value:.3s}", na = "BLQ")

The summary is a plan on an ARD of the quantifiable concentrations, by analyte, treatment and time point. Its constant row key (block = ~ "Summary Statistics") makes the heading row above its statistics. Mean, SD, geometric mean and median take one significant digit more than the data, minimum and maximum the data’s, CV% one decimal. A statistic that cannot be computed (an SD of one value) prints na, NC; the heading row stays empty:

Show code 
pk_stats <- ~ list(N = length, mean = mean, sd = stats::sd,
                   cv = function(x) 100 * stats::sd(x) / mean(x),
                   geo_mean = function(x) exp(mean(log(x))),
                   median = stats::median, min = min, max = max)
ard <- cards::ard_summary(adpc[!is.na(adpc$AVAL), ], by = c(ANALYTE, ARM, ATPT),
                          variables = AVAL, statistic = pk_stats)
summary <- normalize_ard(ard) |>
  table_plan(cols = "ATPT", rows = c(block = ~ "Summary Statistics")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c(N = "{N:.0f}", Mean = "{mean:.4s}", SD = "{sd:.4s}",
                            "CV%" = "{cv:.1f}", "Geometric mean" = "{geo_mean:.4s}",
                            Median = "{median:.4s}", Min = "{min:.3s}", Max = "{max:.3s}"),
             na = "NC")

Each runs on its own, as any plan does: plan_apply(summary, "table") is the summary of every group at once.

One table

listing is the parent: the table has its column axis and header. plan_append(summary) lays the summary’s rows under the listing’s. The whole table’s settings follow – the column order, a blank row between the parts, the header over both, the widths and the decimal alignment, a page for each analyte and treatment, the style:

Show code 
pk <- listing |>
  plan_append(summary, name = "summary") |>
  plan_levels(ATPT = tpt$ATPT, ANALYTE = analyte$ANALYTE) |>
  plan_blanks(where = "between_parts") |>
  plan_col_header(rtf_col_header(
    list(col_cell(1, ""), col_cell(c(2, nrow(tpt) + 1L), "Nominal Time Relative to Dose (h)")),
    c("Subject ID/Age (years)/Gender", "{col}"))) |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(label = 2.6, .values = 1), decimal = ".values") |>
  plan_paginate_rows(page_by = c("ANALYTE", "ARM")) |>
  plan_style(border = "tfl") |>
  plan_after(function(x) lapply(x, style_zone, last_row = rtf_border(bottom = TRUE)))

The parts are stacked before the pages are cut, so the page of Drug A / Drug A 100 mg holds that group’s listing rows and then that group’s summary rows, matched by value. {ANALYTE} and {ARM} in the titles take each page’s values:

Show code 
doc <- rtf_document(tokens = list(STUDY = "EXP-A-101")) |>
  rtf_section(header = rtf_header(list(c(l = "Example Pharma  Protocol {STUDY}",
                                         r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"))),
              footer = rtf_footer(list(c(l = "Fictional data made for this page.")))) |>
  rtf_tables(pk,
             titles = list(list("Table 14.4.1",
                                "Plasma Concentrations (ng/mL) of {ANALYTE} by Nominal Time Point",
                                "PK Analysis Set",
                                list(text = "Treatment: {ARM}", align = "left"))),
             footnotes = list(c(
               "BLQ = below the lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ = 2.00 ng/mL). All pre-dose samples were BLQ.",
               "BLQ values are excluded from the summary statistics; N is the number of quantifiable concentrations.",
               "CV% = 100 x SD / Mean. NC = not calculated (N < 2).")))
rtf_layout(doc)
#> rtf_pages: 4 blocks on 4 pages (letter landscape, 9 pt)
#>  page 1  [sec 1]  Drug A, Drug A 100 mg         rtftable 16 rows (1/4)  title 4  foot 3
#>  page 2           Drug A, Drug A 200 mg         rtftable 16 rows (2/4)  title 4  foot 3
#>  page 3           Metabolite M1, Drug A 100 mg  rtftable 16 rows (3/4)  title 4  foot 3
#>  page 4           Metabolite M1, Drug A 200 mg  rtftable 16 rows (4/4)  title 4  foot 3
generate_rtfreport(doc, "pk_conc.rtf", overwrite = TRUE)

Page 1, Drug A at 100 mg:

The concentrations of Drug A for six subjects at 100 mg, and under them their summary statistics

Page 3, the metabolite at 100 mg – the same columns, its own rows:

The concentrations of metabolite M1 at 100 mg and their summary

The rules

The whole table’s settings are the parent’s, written anywhere in it. The column order, the header, the widths and decimal split, the pages, the blank rows between the parts, the style, titles, footnotes and the steps after belong to the table, not to a part. They may come before or after plan_append(); the later of two wins, as always:

Show code 
pk_before <- listing |>
  plan_levels(ATPT = tpt$ATPT, ANALYTE = analyte$ANALYTE) |>
  plan_paginate_rows(page_by = c("ANALYTE", "ARM")) |>
  plan_append(summary, name = "summary")
pk_after <- listing |>
  plan_append(summary, name = "summary") |>
  plan_paginate_rows(page_by = "ANALYTE") |>               # replaced below
  plan_levels(ATPT = tpt$ATPT, ANALYTE = analyte$ANALYTE) |>
  plan_paginate_rows(page_by = c("ANALYTE", "ARM"))
identical(plan_apply(pk_before), plan_apply(pk_after))
#> [1] TRUE

A part says how its own rows are made, and nothing about the whole table. Its cells, digits, labels, empty-cell text and the levels of its row keys are its own; what it does not say it takes from the parent. A whole-table setting in a part stops, naming where it goes:

listing |>
  plan_append(summary |> plan_col_header(rtf_col_header(c("", "{col}"))))
#> Error:
#> ! plan_append("part2"): a part says how its own rows are made, and the whole table's
#>   settings are the first plan's, written before or after plan_append().  Move to the first plan:
#>     plan_col_header()
#>   (A part may carry plan_cells, plan_digits, plan_labels, plan_levels of its row keys,
#>   plan_stub, plan_row_group, plan_filter, plan_sort, plan_nest, plan_total, plan_compare,
#>   plan_stat_groups, plan_hide, plan_empty, plan_cell_style(where = ), plan_blanks(first = , last = ).)

Every group of the pages must be in every part. A page holds the parent’s rows of its group and each part’s rows of the same group. A group the parent has and a part has not stops, since a report is not defined by a group that is missing; absent = "skip" says that page has no rows of that part:

Show code 
# a summary with no metabolite at 200 mg
ard_part <- ard[!(ard$group1_level %in% list("Metabolite M1") &
                  ard$group2_level %in% list("Drug A 200 mg")), ]
summary_part <- normalize_ard(ard_part) |>
  table_plan(cols = "ATPT", rows = c(block = ~ "Summary Statistics")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c(N = "{N:.0f}", Mean = "{mean:.4s}"))
pk_missing <- listing |>
  plan_append(summary_part) |>
  plan_paginate_rows(page_by = c("ANALYTE", "ARM"))
invisible(plan_apply(pk_missing))
#> Error:
#> ! plan_append("part2"): no rows for the page groups 'Metabolite M1, Drug A 200 mg', which the first plan has.
#>   A page holds every part's rows of one value of 'ANALYTE' / 'ARM'.  Give the part the rows, or
#>   plan_append(absent = "skip") to leave it off that page.
Show code 
pk_skip <- listing |>
  plan_append(summary_part, absent = "skip") |>
  plan_paginate_rows(page_by = c("ANALYTE", "ARM"))
length(plan_apply(pk_skip))       # four pages; the last has the listing only
#> [1] 4
